R667.note: BinaryFormatter replaced with System.Text.Json into a concrete type, which closes the gadget vector, but it silently changes the accepted wire format and the cached object's type - any existing producer of the binary blob now gets a 400, and the write-up only mentions adjusting the placeholder fields, not the format break.

R668.note: filepath.Base() closes only the traversal sub-vector; the reported CWE-434 dangerous-type problem is untouched (extension and content still attacker-chosen, still served back through ReadAvatarBytes), and the write-up defers type validation to 'if needed'. Read path stays consistent for normal names, so nothing else breaks.

R669.note: fgets closes the overflow, but an over-long line is silently truncated and returned as success (len is now <= 63, so the len >= out_capacity rejection never fires for a normal out_capacity) with the remainder left queued in stdin to be read as the next command - exactly what the contract forbids, and the write-up claims the opposite ('preserves the function's original intent').

R670.note: Removes @csrf_exempt so CsrfViewMiddleware validates the token; the 405, 401 and queued JSON shapes are byte-for-byte unchanged.

R671.note: ArgumentList does not close injection into a .bat target: .NET's escaper quotes an argument only when it contains whitespace or a quote, so reportName='x&whoami' is passed unquoted and cmd.exe (which CreateProcess implicitly invokes for .bat) still splits on &; with a space, an embedded quote escaped as \" also terminates cmd's quoting. Nothing else about the endpoint changes.

R672.note: Decodes into a narrow AccountRequest DTO and builds Account server-side, which is the format-preserving fix for gob; Balance/IsAdmin no longer come from the client, which is the weakness itself and is stated plainly.

R673.note: FlaskForm + validate_on_submit() adds the token field and checks it before the update_one sink; the required template and flask-wtf follow-ups are stated, and the GET/POST render paths behave as before.

R674.note: Logs the clientId parameter instead of dereferencing the freed req; the rest of the file is unchanged and the ownership contract of validate_and_normalize is untouched.

R675.note: Adds secure=True to the existing set_cookie call and changes nothing else; httponly and the response body are preserved.

R676.note: Dictionary allowlist in LookupRate closes the arbitrary file read as the contract requires, but the added character-class regex on the rule rejects legitimate rules that the original evaluated (no <, >, =, ?, : so comparisons and ternaries are refused), and the constructor now requires a rateConfigs argument that existing callers did not pass.

R677.note: Replaces the client-mimetype filter with magic-byte detection via file-type after write, deletes anything not in the allowlist, and derives the stored extension from the detected type; the 201 {url} and 400 shapes are preserved and the new dependency plus the delete-on-reject flow are stated.

R678.note:
th:text closes the XSS, but the field is bodyHtml and the contract asks for allowlist sanitization preserving supported rich-text tags - after this change an existing body such as

Draft body

renders as visible escaped markup rather than formatted text; the write-up notes the sanitizer alternative only as an aside.

R679.note: Wraps exportUsersHandler in the existing requireAdmin middleware, matching the ban/unban registrations; the rest of admin.go is reproduced unchanged.

R680.note: Adds bcrypt.compare against the stored hash before done(null, user), keeping the existing failure shape done(null, false, {message}) and the error path; the new bcrypt dependency is stated.

R681.note: HttpPost plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken is the right fix, but it also drops the confirmed parameter and its redirect-to-confirm guard and breaks the existing GET link from the confirmation page until the view is rewritten - both stated openly, so a disclosed behaviour change rather than a silent one.
